items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I did my first major gig with Kenny Burrell in Detroit, at Baker’s Keyboard Lounge.

ctx.x: He wrote “Cloudburst,” and he was also the arranger of a famous R&B tune called “Our Day Will Come,” Ruby and the Romantics. So I became kind of his protégé. Because his son felt I should meet his father. And he lived right down the block from the school, so a lot of times after, instead of going home I’d go to his house. And he’d have me rehearsing with some of the singers that would come by the crib, he took me to sessions, I met Kenny Burrell through him, I met Jerome Richardson through him, because he was…
Let me take you back for a minute, what led you to the piano, and was your family supportive of your music?
